subject: Staged reserve migration & throughput commitment for Halloway - renewal discussion
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <ops@halloway.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 26 Feb 2027 18:12:00 -0800
Subject: Proposal: staged reserve migration and throughput commitments for renewal

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for the call earlier. As Halloway approaches the March renewal, I wanted to put a concrete, low-friction proposal on the table so your team can evaluate operational and commercial impact for moving from the current 16-GPU reserved pool to a 32-GPU reserved configuration. High level recommendations are attached (RL-Scale-Proposal-0327.pdf) but key points below: 

- Staged migration over 6 weeks to minimize disruption (two 8-GPU phases).
- Blended reserved per-GPU hourly rate with a 12-month term.
- Throughput commitment: sustained baseline throughput for the full pool, with burst headroom for scheduled spikes.
- Optional canary region (eu) to validate traffic patterns before full swap.

Requested next steps:
1) Can you confirm renewal target date (you mentioned early March)?
2) Who should receive the commercial worksheet (procurement contact) — I’ve copied Jordan for pricing details.
3) Any required security or compliance artifacts we should bundle with the amendment?

Attaching a short ratecard and a high-level rollout playbook for your ops team. Happy to hop on a 30-minute call to walk through.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: RL-Scale-Proposal-0327.pdf (proposal, 6 pages); reserved-ratecard-32gpu.xlsx (rate table)
From: Elena Morales <ops@halloway.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 27 Feb 2027 09:04:12 -0500
Subject: Re: Proposal: staged reserve migration and throughput commitments for renewal

Marcus —

Thanks for the clear summary. A few questions up front:

- Renewal target: Mar 10 (end of our current term) — procurement lead is Samir (copied his team on the thread separately).
- Can you confirm the guaranteed throughput numbers (tokens/minute or requests/sec) that map to the baseline? Our SREs need a concrete SLA to validate capacity planning.
- How does burst headroom work from an accounting perspective? Do bursts consume reserved hours or bill as on-demand?

Also, we’ll want a short runbook for rollback in case inference latency regresses during the second phase. Can you include that?

Elena Morales
Head of Platform Operations, Halloway AI
ops@halloway.ai
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <ops@halloway.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 27 Feb 2027 10:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposal: staged reserve migration and throughput commitments for renewal

Elena —

Great — Mar 10 works as a target. Quick answers while I loop in Jordan (pricing) and Neha (reliability):

- Throughput commitments: We guarantee a baseline of 1.2M tokens/min sustained across the 32-GPU pool (measured as aggregate p50 throughput for your current model mix). For latency-sensitive paths we’ll maintain p95 token latency <= 70ms for the baseline config.
- Burst headroom: Scheduled bursts (up to 25% of pool capacity for up to 4 hours) are covered under the reserved commitment; unscheduled bursts beyond that are billable at the on-demand per-GPU hourly rate and will be visible in the usage dashboard.
- Rollback runbook: included in RL-Scale-Proposal-0327.pdf (section 4) — stepwise switch-back with KV cache invalidation window and traffic split percentages.

Jordan — can you surface the blended per-hour numbers (old vs proposed) and the change in hourly commit we’d need for a Mar 10 effective date?

Thanks,
Marcus

Onward,
Marcus Lin
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <ops@halloway.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 28 Feb 2027 14:30:00 -0800
Subject: Halloway pricing worksheet & blended reserved rates (16 -> 32)

Hi Elena —

Thanks for the quick replies. See the attached reserved-ratecard-32gpu.xlsx for the full worksheet; summary pricing below (12-month reserved term, billed monthly):

- Current committed pool: 16 GPUs at $3.10 / GPU / hour = $49.60 / hour baseline
- Proposed committed pool: 32 GPUs at blended $2.60 / GPU / hour = $83.20 / hour baseline
- Effective blended on-boarding discount for year 1: additional 8% off listed reserved rates if signed by Mar 10 (applies to the whole 32-GPU commitment).
- Burst (unscheduled overage): billed at on-demand $4.40 / GPU / hour; scheduled burst (pre-booked) falls under the committed rate for the duration of the window.

Operationally we recommend a staged billing start: first 16 GPUs transition to the new reserved SKU immediately; second tranche (weeks 3-6) is brought online and prorated in month 1. That minimizes invoice churn and gives Halloway two full weeks of telemetry before the full 32 is in effect.

If you’re happy with the numbers I can generate an amendment (DocuSign) that codifies: term, per-hour reserved rate, burst rules, and the throughput SLA language Marcus shared.

Jordan Blake
Account Director, Redwood Inference

Attachments: reserved-ratecard-32gpu.xlsx
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <ops@halloway.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 01 Mar 2027 11:00:00 -0800
Subject: Operational notes for staged migration + throughput validation

Elena / team —

Two operational items to call out from the SRE side: 

1) Canary plan: we recommend a cross-regional canary (10% traffic, eu region) for 72 hours. During that window we’ll capture model-level latency and KV hit rates. Failure conditions include sustained p95 regression > 15% or error-rate > 0.5% for 1 hour.

2) Metrics & observability: we’ll provide pre-configured dashboards (token throughput, request latencies by route, per-GPU utilization) and an exported CSV with baseline metrics (throughput-benchmark-summary.csv) so your SREs can run differential checks.

3) Rollback mechanics: traffic split rollback is handled at the routing layer. Cache warmup during rollback will take ~8 minutes for your average prompt mix; we recommend a short maintenance window if you anticipate rollback.

Happy to run a dry-run with your SREs this week.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Samir Khan <procurement@halloway.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Morales <ops@halloway.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 02 Mar 2027 14:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposal: staged reserve migration and throughput commitments for renewal

Team —

Thanks — the numbers look reasonable and the operational safeguards are acceptable to our SREs. Two quick commercial asks before we sign:

- Please include the 8% onboarding discount in the DocuSign amendment and show the first-month prorated invoice reflecting a two-tranche start (16 GPUs -> add 16 GPUs mid-month).
- Can you confirm a 30‑day notice window for any rate changes mid-term?

If you can update the amendment with those two items I’ll get the internal approval routed this afternoon and we can execute by COB.

Samir Khan
Procurement Manager, Halloway AI
procurement@halloway.ai

--
Requested action: Jordan to generate DocuSign amendment with (a) blended $2.60/GPU/hr for 32 GPUs, (b) onboarding 8% discount for year 1, (c) prorated first-month invoicing with staged activation, (d) explicit 30-day notice for rate changes, (e) SLA clauses per Marcus/Neha and the rollback runbook attached.
